build.summary: CI selection v3 (OD-L1-19/20/21) is implemented in tools/ci/select_tests.py. For each target it records compile inputs (rustc dep-info), executed files (coverage), and read/dirs/absent paths (strace through cargo's runner with a seccomp filter), plus each package's library inputs. Rules 1-9 are in: image and PR-base full triggers, noop/body/structural classification, a directory rule, unmapped targets run, filtered baseline failures, and examples. The literal matcher is gone. Negative controls now run measured through a new `control` subcommand, and their failures are merged into outcome.failed. Workflows: test jobs queue instead of cancelling, strace is installed, python3 -u, branch passed through env, overwrite on upload, a self-test step. The A1 closure step is removed. The checker fix for F-08 is in. Verified: self-test passes and flags 25 problems in the v2 workflows. A local measured run of 7 targets plus 1 example passed with 0 entries lost; it found a strace_works bug, now fixed. 15/15 selection cases pass, plus the control and fake-gh probes, reachability 99/99, YAML parse and the loop checker. Of the 26 findings, 25 are fixed and F12 is not applicable. Rulings R1-R23 are in V3_NOTES.md; TRIAGE section 11 is written in Korean.

R9 follows the design literally: a body change always selects the owning package's own lib/bin unit tests, because their dep-info lists every source of the crate. The alternative is to exempt them as for noop changes; the owner can choose that.

On the two negative cases: every crates/*/src file is read by generic_scope_contracts. So a comment-only change in a member source selects that one reader; it selects nothing only if that reader is removed (case N1-no-reader). A body change also selects the reader and the package's own lib unit tests (case N2).

Gaps that remain and are documented in TRIAGE 11.5: doc tests are not measured (no file access found in member doc comments); a noop change shifts spans (line!, panic locations); auto-trait leakage through body changes; inputs read only in some runs; build-script rerun inputs are not recorded; tests filtered with --skip other than the declared controls; reads that strace cannot see.
F14: no periodic full run, by owner decision OD-L1-21(4). A missed change is revisited only by the full suite before release.

reviews.summary: Reviewed b0d4bc97 read-and-run. Lens findings: F1-F13 closed (F12 N/A), F14 partly (image trigger added; path filters unchanged, no periodic run by owner). With v3 decide() and the builder's measured map, replays of 95d589e86 and ee138227 and cases F3-F7 select the named targets; a sweep of 1040 compile-time links of 588 units (w2-v24 dep-info) under noop/body/structural misses only own-crate lib/bin unit tests on noop (R8, by design). Probes: coverage attributes macro-generated and include!d fn regions to their own files; strace -ff -y traces children, cwd, stat/ls/absent probes. No major hole. Minor holes: (1) tokenizer drops operator spacing: '&&'->'& &' or '=>'->'= >' is noop, so executing targets are skipped; (2) path filters omit measured inputs (docs/, research/, fixtures/, tools/, .cargo/); (3) listing rule judges directory existence on PR heads, not the merge tree; (4) .gitattributes not global though it changes checked-out bytes; (5) mkdir/rename/unlink/utimensat/failed chdir untraced; (6) noop/doc-test invariants unenforced. Scope clean: allowed paths only, protected files untouched.

findings.claim: The change classifier loses the spacing between punctuation characters. A whitespace-only edit that splits or joins a multi-character operator is therefore classified noop. Noop ignores executed sets and own-crate unit tests, so the targets that run the changed code are not selected.
findings.evidence: rust_tokens emits every punctuation character as its own token (tools/ci/select_tests.py:342). classify_texts compares only (kind, value) (403-405). scripts/tok_probe.py classifies all of these as noop: '1 => 2' to '1 = > 2', 'check(x) && check(x)' to 'check(x) & &check(x)', '(0..5)' to '(0. .5)', '-> usize' to '- > usize', '+= 1' to '+ = 1'. With the measured map (scripts/joint_punct_decide.py), changing crates/rodas5p-integrators/src/integrate.rs:1057 'if success && collector.is_complete()' to 'if success & &collector.is_complete()' gives noop. It selects only the text readers generic_scope_contracts, ppsw1_6b_contracts and ptsw2b_contracts, not cli alg02_predictive_controller, which executes integrate.rs. '& &' evaluates the right operand unconditionally. The split forms are syntax errors that no selected target compiles when the file's crate has no other selected target (fair-ab, cli or vigilode sources: only the integrators reader runs).
findings.fix: Keep punctuation spacing in rust_tokens. For example, emit ('p', c + ('j' if the next character is punctuation else ''), line), or classify as body or structural any change of whitespace next to a punctuation token. Add the five probe pairs to self-test.

findings.claim: The trigger path filters of both test workflows still exclude inputs that v3 measures. A pull request whose whole diff lies outside them, or a push to main that touches only them, runs no test job, so the tests that read those inputs are not run on that change (F14 residual).
findings.evidence: production.yml:26-42 and ignored-tests.yml:21-37 list crates/**, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, rust-toolchain.toml (missing from ignored-tests' push list, as is ignored-tests.yml itself), the workflow and tools/ci/**. The measured map has inputs outside these paths: docs/CONSTANTS_PROVENANCE.toml, FROZEN_ZETA34_POLICY.json and two other research files (constants_provenance_contracts), research/stiff_native_benchmark_20261001/NATIVE.json (alg02), fixtures/rodas5p_coefficients_snapshot.json (core library input) and tools/reference_v2/generate_references_v2.py (fair-ab library input). 56 production-scope test or src files name research/, docs/, fixtures/ or tools/ paths; for example, r3_certified_budget_contracts reads fixtures/r3_certified_budget_fixtures.json. .cargo/ is a global prefix of the selector but not a trigger path. Pull-request filters use the three-dot PR diff, so the gap is data/docs-only PRs and main pushes. Those changes wait for a later pr_base change or crates/** push, and no periodic run exists.
findings.fix: Add research/**, docs/**, fixtures/**, tools/**, .cargo/** and **/.gitattributes to the pull_request and push paths of both workflows. Also add rust-toolchain.toml and ignored-tests.yml to the push list of ignored-tests. A selection with no affected target finishes in minutes.

findings.claim: For an added path, the listing rule decides directory existence on the PR head trees and checks the directories that the change creates only against absent. A directory that exists in the tested merge tree only through the base branch, and that a test listed, never selects that test.
findings.evidence: select() passes the baseline head and HEAD_SHA (PR heads) to existing_dirs (select_tests.py:997-1001), while the map is measured on GitHub's merge commit (R15). decide() puts directories missing at the base head into created (863-880). For status A, match_inputs checks created only against absent (790-793); only D checks read and dirs (794-797). Repro scripts/merge_tree_listing.py: an entry with dirs {research/new} and the change A research/new/x.json, with head trees lacking research/new, selects nothing. No current test lists such a directory: generic_scope_contracts lists crates/ and default_path_golden lists its golden dir.
findings.fix: In match_inputs, apply the D check to A as well: select when any created directory is in dirs or read.

findings.claim: A .gitattributes change alters the checked-out bytes of unchanged files without any blob change. It is neither global nor read by any target, so tests that hash or byte-compare those files are not selected.
findings.evidence: is_global (select_tests.py:258-259; GLOBAL_FILES/PREFIXES 90-91) has no .gitattributes. Scratch repo review-soundness/gitattr_probe_1: adding '*.json text eol=crlf' gives the diff 'A .gitattributes' only, while a fresh checkout of the unchanged x.json changes from sha256 b77a0d61... to 99768b46.... 28 production-scope test files use sha256 pins (e.g. constants_provenance_contracts), and research/rigorous_performance_audit_20261027/.gitattributes exists.
findings.fix: Treat .gitattributes at any depth as a global file, i.e. os.path.basename(path) == '.gitattributes' in is_global.

findings.claim: Path system calls whose result depends on existence or metadata are not traced: mkdir, rename, link, unlink, utimensat, chmod, truncate, statfs, xattr, and a failed chdir. A test that decides on them has no absent or read entry, and adding or removing that path does not select it (latent).
findings.evidence: TRACED (select_tests.py:95-96) covers open/openat/openat2/creat, execve(at), the stat family, the access family, readlink(at), chdir and fchdir. trace_events ignores failed chdir/fchdir (660-665). Examples: fs::create_dir returning AlreadyExists, rename with RENAME_NOREPLACE, a failing set_current_dir with ENOENT. The probe trace review-soundness/probe_strace/t.* shows the mkdir of 'mkdir -p' unrecorded. grep finds no member test applying these calls to repository paths today.
findings.fix: Add ?mkdir,mkdirat,?rename,renameat,?renameat2,?link,linkat,?symlink,symlinkat,?unlink,unlinkat,?rmdir,utimensat,?chmod,fchmodat,?truncate,?statfs,?getxattr,?lgetxattr,?listxattr,?llistxattr to TRACED, with the at-variants in AT_SYSCALLS and both paths parsed for rename and link. Record ENOENT or ENOTDIR as absent and any other result as read. Record a failed chdir with ENOENT or ENOTDIR as absent.

findings.claim: The noop rule and the unmeasured doc tests are sound only under invariants that nothing enforces. One later commit can make comment-only changes or doc tests silently unselected (latent).
findings.evidence: R8 (V3_NOTES.md:70-82) and R10 (90-94) assume three things. First, no assertion depends on line!/column!/file!/Location::caller/track_caller or panic locations. Second, no member's src include_str!s or include_bytes!s a .rs file (an own-crate text consumer that noop exempts). Third, no doc comment accesses repository files. My grep confirms all three today: no hits for any. self_test (select_tests.py:1555-1938) and check_workflows (1505-1552) test only selector functions and workflow text.
findings.fix: Add a self-test check that greps member sources and fails on line!(), column!(), Location::caller, #[track_caller], include_str!/include_bytes! of a .rs path under src/, and fs:: or include_* inside doc comments. Alternatively, classify a noop change that shifts line numbers in such a file as body.

reviews.summary:
Reviewed b0d4bc97, lens CI mechanics. All 12 mechanics findings from v1 are closed: job-level queueing, required-features and stale targets never named (reproduced), failed controls merged and reselected (probe), pr_base trigger, A1 step removed, -u/flush, control fails on a missing selection, the F-08 probe, listing notes, limits kept, overwrite, branch via env. Self-test, a 2-target measured run on the real repo (0 lost) and the loop checker pass. All changed paths are allowed.
New findings:
(1) major: the image trigger compares ImageVersion, but hosted ubuntu-latest serves 20261116.88.1 and .202.1 at the same time, even within one run, so about 3 runs in 10 go full.
(2) major: dropping the A1 test step leaves about 186 non-ignored cli and fair-ab tests with no CI.
(3) minor: dispatch and PR baselines force full runs; the path filters miss measured inputs outside crates/**; the listing has no head_repository filter; strace installs via apt every run; v2 hosted coverage runs already exceed v1 durations (>122 min).

earlier_findings.evidence: No workflow-level concurrency remains (yaml parse: top-level None in all three workflows). The test job has group production-test-${{ github.ref }} with cancel-in-progress false (production.yml:114-116); ignored-tests is the same (ignored-tests.yml:60-62). The short jobs keep their own cancelling groups (production.yml:73-75, 91-93, 178-180, 221-223, 254-256). GitHub keeps one pending job per group, so pushes coalesce, and the baseline is the newest complete run with id < current (select_tests.py:1456-1459). check_workflows passes in the self-test. Caveat: a workflow_dispatch run has ref refs/heads/<branch>, a different group, so it can overlap with PR runs.

Reproduced the original case against v3 with real cargo metadata via decide(): an edit of tests/audit2_structured_correction_contracts.rs plus baseline failures audit0930_reuse_certificate_contracts (unmet features) and gone_contracts (deleted). Selected: only the real baseline failure. Both were dropped with notes ('requires the features audit2-research', 'no longer a test target'). Full-mode units of integrators name 0 of the 5 unmet targets (280 units). Same as F10.

Scratch-workspace probe (review-CI/mini1-out). A control with the wrong signature exited 1 and wrote b:fail to failed-controls.txt. run merged it into outcome.failed with negative_control true (complete true). The next select added b:fail ('failed in the baseline run (negative control)'), so the control step would run again. Upload stays !cancelled(). Same as F9.

Closed by the owner-chosen alternative. PR_BASE=github.event.pull_request.base.sha is recorded (production.yml:126,156; select_tests.py:970-972), and a different base gives a full run (probe: 'pull-request base changed ... -> 33ba6347', full). The checkout is still the merge commit. Unverified on hosted data: whether payload base.sha always equals the merge's base (the base branch has not moved since 11-16). Same as F8.

The diff of a1-inner-tolerance-parity.yml removes exactly the 3 lines of step 'Run the workspace test closure'; the other steps are unchanged. See new finding N2: this leaves cli and fair-ab normal tests with no CI run.

Every selector and checker step uses python3 -u (production.yml:145,149,156,160; ignored-tests.yml:88,90,94,100,114,126,133). stream() flushes each line, including rendered diagnostics (select_tests.py:1149-1155). Probe logs stream test output line by line.

The workflows no longer call has; the control steps call 'select_tests.py control'. With a missing selection.json, control exits 1 (FileNotFoundError; review-CI/f07/log), so the step fails instead of printing 'not run'.

Reproduced on a git-archive export (review-CI/checker-probe). Unmodified: 99/99 reachable. An #[ignore] test added in crates/vigilode-bench/tests is reported as 'ignored tests not run by any workflow' (exit 1). The --workspace match is now limited to member dirs (check_ignored_tests_in_ci.py:113-114).

A listing failure gets its own note with stderr (select_tests.py:1452-1454). A download failure other than 'no valid artifacts found' is listed in errors and counted in the note (1466-1471, 1494-1496). The self-test fake-gh cases (HTTP 403 listing, HTTP 502 download) pass; I ran the self-test, exit 0.

The raised limits are kept: test 300, ignored 330 (yaml parse). Risk remains: the live hosted v2 runs at a66215e7 (coverage, per-target, no strace) are test job of run 45378440406 and ignored job of run 45378440571. At 12:52 UTC both were still in their run step after 122-123 min, longer than every completed v1 full run (test 92-109, ignored 94-97 min). v3 adds strace and an apt install. See N7.
overwrite: true is set on both uploads (production.yml:173, ignored-tests.yml:144).

BRANCH, HEAD_SHA, PR_BASE and FULL are job env vars (production.yml:124-127, ignored-tests.yml:70-73). The scripts use "$BRANCH" etc. and no ${{ github.head_ref }} appears in any run script. The REST query is urlencoded (select_tests.py:1449). The self-test passes branch 'x;$(false)' as data.

findings.claim: Rule 1 compares ImageVersion exactly. Hosted ubuntu-latest serves at least two image versions at once, so consecutive runs often differ and run the whole suite (coverage + strace) with no code change, defeating OD-L1-19 for roughly 3 runs in 10.
findings.evidence:
select_tests.py:947-950 and 970-972 compare ImageVersion. Set-up-job logs (read-only gh api; review-CI/hosted/image_versions.tsv, ignored_job_images.tsv):
- Run 45358324432, jobs started 2026-11-24T08:41:48Z: fmt on 20261116.88.1, clippy and docs on 20261116.202.1.
- Runs 45163804110, 45187691774 and 45221470766 are mixed the same way.
- ignored-tests job of run 45221470637 (16:53) ran on .88.1, between runs on .202.1.
- 7 of 39 sampled ubuntu-latest jobs (11-23 11:17 to 11-24 09:04) ran on .88.1, so P(consecutive runs differ) is about 0.29.
- The version also changes weekly (20261111.196.1 on 11-16/17).
Probe with the same baseline: ImageVersion .202.1 gives 'selected'; .88.1 gives 'runner image version changed since the baseline: 20261116.202.1 -> 20261116.88.1', full.
findings.fix: Ask the owner what 'runner image' in OD-L1-21(1) means. Options: trigger on ImageOS only (optionally with a pinned runs-on label), keeping ImageVersion as information; or compare a fingerprint of what tests depend on (e.g. libc/libm package versions). Add a self-test case for two concurrent versions.

findings.claim: Removing the A1 step 'Run the workspace test closure' leaves about 186 non-ignored tests of rodas5p-cli and rodas5p-fair-ab with no CI run. The v1 premise 'Production CI and Ignored long tests cover the workspace' is false for these packages.
findings.evidence:
- Production test scope is core, krylov, integrators, vigilode, vigilode-coupled (production.yml:156); ignored-tests runs only --ignored.
- A grep of all 31 workflows finds only 2 cli targets in A1 (a1-inner-tolerance-parity.yml:64-68) and 2 fair-ab targets in audit2 (tools/check-audit2-readiness.sh:22).
- Crude #[test] count: cli 92 non-ignored (4 still run), fair-ab 116 (18 still run).
- Hosted A1 run 45358324393 (2f663808) ran them in the removed step, 08:54-09:50 UTC: tests/cli_contracts.rs, triage_cli.rs, fair_ab_contracts.rs, paired_timing_contracts.rs and others (review-CI/hosted/a1_45358324393.log).
- production.yml:59-60 still says 'rodas5p-cli is tested in a1-inner-tolerance-parity.yml'.
findings.fix: Take this back to the owner under OD-L1-21(3). Either add a normal-mode selected run for rodas5p-cli and rodas5p-fair-ab (a scoped selection step or job with its own artifact), or record that these tests run only in the release full suite. Correct the production.yml comment either way.

findings.claim: A workflow_dispatch baseline (pr_base None) forces the next PR run to be full, and the reverse also holds. A manual full dispatch on a PR branch (the input defaults to full) is followed by a second full PR run.
findings.evidence: full_reasons treats None as a value (select_tests.py:947-950). The run listing has no event filter (select_tests.py:1449-1458), and PR_BASE is empty for dispatch (production.yml:126). Probe case 3: baseline environment pr_base None, PR run with a base gives 'pull-request base changed since the baseline: None -> 33ba6347...', full. The full run is needed for soundness, since dispatch tests the branch tree and PR tests the merge tree, but it can be avoided by not using such baselines.
findings.fix: Filter the listing to runs of the current event (the event= query parameter, or r['event'] == GITHUB_EVENT_NAME). PR runs then take only PR runs as baseline, and the base trigger stays for real base changes.

findings.claim: The trigger path filters do not cover measured inputs outside crates/**. A push that changes only such inputs triggers neither job, so the change is tested only at a later triggered push; on main, not until the next crates/** push. This gap is not listed in TRIAGE 11.5.
findings.evidence:
- production.yml:26-42 and ignored-tests.yml:21-37 cover crates/**, the manifests, the lock file, the toolchain file, tools/ci/** and the workflow file, plus one research path in ignored-tests.
- The F1 replay commit 95d589e8 touches only research/reaudit_accuracy_speed_20261010/gain_witness.rs, which is in the compile set of core residual_gain_contract.
- docs/CONSTANTS_PROVENANCE.toml, the FROZEN_ZETA34_POLICY.json read and fixtures/rodas5p_coefficients_snapshot.json are also measured inputs (v3_logs/e2e_map.json).
- The global prefix .cargo/ (select_tests.py:91) is not a trigger either.
findings.fix: Widen the pull_request/push paths (e.g. the whole repository with paths-ignore for record-only directories), or have the owner accept and document the deferral.

findings.claim: The baseline lookup accepts any run whose head_branch matches. On this public repository, a fork PR from a branch with the same name could upload an outcome and map that the owner's next run uses, selecting nothing. This is pre-existing since v1, but in v3 the map steers the selection.
findings.evidence: select_tests.py:1449-1458 filters only by branch and run id. Run objects carry head_repository. The repo is public; forks_count is 0 today, so the risk is theoretical. All 100 listed runs come from cosmosapjw-quantum/vigilode.
findings.fix: Keep only runs with head_repository.full_name == GITHUB_REPOSITORY, together with the event filter of N3.

findings.claim: Every test job depends on apt to install strace. An apt failure fails the job before the self-test, baseline and select steps, although R18 makes a missing strace a degraded but valid mode of the selector.
findings.evidence: actions/runner-images images/ubuntu/toolsets/toolset-2604.json lists no strace, and ubuntu-latest jobs ran on ubuntu-26.04. The install step runs apt-get update && install without continue-on-error (production.yml:137-140, ignored-tests.yml:83-86).
findings.fix: Add continue-on-error: true (or a retry) to the install step. The selector then records 'strace is not installed', and rule 5 reruns the targets that lost their entries.

findings.claim: The duration of a hosted full run is still unknown, and the available evidence points up. Together with N1, more full runs bring a run close to the 300/330-minute limits; a timeout leaves no outcome, so the next run is full again.
findings.evidence: The live v2 runs (coverage, per-target commands, no strace) are test job of run 45378440406 and ignored job of run 45378440571. At 12:52 UTC both were in their run step after 122-123 min (review-CI/hosted/v2_progress.tsv), longer than all completed v1 full runs (test 92-109, ignored 94-97 min). Local per-target measurement overhead is small: profraw 0.9 MB, trace 312 KB, llvm-cov export 0.34 s and 166 MB.
findings.fix: Record the final durations of these two runs before merging. If a full run uses more than about two thirds of the limit, split the full mode or raise the limits within the 360-minute cap for hosted jobs.

findings.claim: The self-test both test jobs run reads and checks the unrelated a1-inner-tolerance-parity.yml. Renaming or deleting that workflow makes the Production and Ignored test jobs fail at the self-test step.
findings.evidence: select_tests.py:1519 opens a1-inner-tolerance-parity.yml unconditionally, and 1550 asserts on its content; the self-test runs in CI (production.yml:145, ignored-tests.yml:90).
findings.fix: Skip the A1 check when the file is missing (os.path.exists), or move the workflow checks to a separate step that does not gate the test selection.

findings.claim: The same-image baseline search (R24) downloads the artifact of every listed run until it finds a qualifying run on the current image. On the first run on a new image, or on a minority image whose last run is far back, that means up to 100 downloads per job, even when the selection then goes full anyway. b0d4bc97 downloaded one.
findings.evidence: recheck/scan_cost.log uses a fake gh with 100 complete runs on 20261116.202.1. A current run on 20261123.5.1 makes 100 downloads (b0d4bc97: 1). A current run on .88.1, whose only .88.1 run is 40 runs back, makes 39 downloads (b0d4bc97: 1). GH_DEBUG=api against the real repository: one gh run download is 2 REST requests (runs/{id}/artifacts and artifacts/{id}/zip) and takes about 1.7 s; a run without the artifact costs 1 request (recheck/ratelimit/dbg*.log). With three selecting jobs, a push on a new image can use about 600 of the GITHUB_TOKEN budget of 1,000 requests per hour per repository, plus about 3 minutes per job. The reviewer's samples show 3 image versions within 8 days. Once the budget runs out, listings and downloads fail and those runs go full.
findings.fix: Find candidates without downloading them. For example, put ImageOS/ImageVersion in the artifact name and list candidates with one call to GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/actions/artifacts?name=<name>, which returns the workflow_run id, head_branch and head_sha. Then download only the chosen run. Alternatively, go full without scanning when no listed run has an artifact for this image. Also skip the lookup when FULL is true (main, dispatch with full).
